senses.definition: Something or someone which creates or makes something.
examples: Kenneth E. Iverson was the creator of APL.

senses.definition: (social media) Ellipsis of content creator, someone who regularly produces and publishes content on social media, especially of a monetizable nature.

quotes.text: People have viewed his videos more than 13 billion times. And last year as the pandemic raged, he became the most-subscribed YouTube creator in the country.
quotes.reference: 2021 May 4, Taylor Lorenz, “Mr. Beast, YouTube Star, Wants to Take Over the Business World”, in The New York Times, →ISSN:

quotes.text: The video shows TikTok creator Harrison Pawluk approaching the woman, Maree, in a public shopping centre.
quotes.reference: 2022 July 14, Rafqa Touma, “Melbourne woman ‘dehumanised’ by viral TikTok filmed without her consent”, in The Guardian:

quotes.text: She wore crimson leggings, a stack of candy-colored beaded necklaces, and a black sweatshirt that read SELF-EMPLOYED because she is a full-time influencer — or “creator,” as it is more polite to say in this part of town.

senses.definition: (religion, sometimes capitalized) The deity that created the world.
(sports) A player who creates opportunities for their team to score goals; a playmaker.

quotes.text: Hernández is not a creator and suffered from a lack of service in previous seasons.
quotes.reference: 2019 July 3, Andrea Canales, Jonathan Tannenwald, “Pulisic, McKennie show plenty of promise for U.S. in Gold Cup”, in The Philadelphia Inquirer:

quotes.text: There have been times this season when it seemed Liverpool were trying to reinvent Salah, the scorer supreme, as a creator and this was a sudden reminder of his greatest strength.
